claims.text: Variation in pre-cooling vacancy density causes the diverse secondary phases observed during cooling and aging of Cr39Co18Fe18Ni18Al7.
Pre-cooling vacancies act as heterogeneous nucleation sites that alter phase-transformation pathways.
The initial Cr39Co18Fe18Ni18Al7 material is in a high-temperature BCC phase.
The initial BCC phase inherently contains vacancies and associated lattice defects.
Changing pre-annealing duration at a fixed high temperature will systematically change the vacancy concentration before cooling.
After pre-annealing, samples will be subjected to an identical cooling rate and isothermal hold at 700 °C.
Pre-annealing generates defect clusters associated with vacancy density.
Vacancy-associated defect clusters serve as heterogeneous nucleation sites.
Higher vacancy populations enhance atomic mobility.
Higher vacancy populations provide energetically favorable sites for secondary-phase nucleation during cooling and aging.
Lower vacancy density produces fewer nucleation sites.
Fewer vacancy-related nucleation sites result in less phase separation.
Longer pre-annealing produces higher vacancy concentrations than minimal pre-annealing.
Longer-pre-annealed samples will exhibit a greater diversity of secondary phases than the baseline.
Longer-pre-annealed samples will exhibit a greater fraction of secondary phases than the baseline.
Recovery during subsequent thermal exposure can erase or mask the effects of initial vacancy concentration.
The vacancy mechanism is expected to be dominant under controlled pre-annealing conditions.

contradictions.description: The material is defined as being in its high-temperature BCC phase, but pre-annealing is specified as occurring above the BCC stability region or above the BCC range. Taken literally, that treatment would place the sample outside the stated BCC phase field rather than merely tune vacancies within the initial BCC state.
